tier_reason: First-party README chart (images/gflops_apple_m4.png) with per-operation GFLOP/s on a named CPU (Apple M4), but no matrix sizes, compiler flags or OpenBLAS version for the run, and the repo's test/performance/benchmark_cblas.py only times whichever library it loads, so not A.

corrections.claimed_speedup: README chart (Apple M4, f32, single thread): GEMM 111.0 vs OpenBLAS 109.9 GFLOP/s (1.01x, derived from page data), SYMM 109.7 vs 109.5, SYRK 109.4 vs 108.8, SYR2K 109.4 vs 109.0, TRSM 100.9 vs 100.2, TRMM 95.8 vs 110.3 (0.87x, slower). README text: matches single-threaded OpenBLAS on 5 of 6 L3 operations and 'slightly outperforms OpenBLAS', ~80% of peak for single-threaded GEMM; generic cache-tiled baseline 6.0-6.3 GFLOP/s (about 17-18x below MuBLIS, derived from page data; README says '~20x').
corrections.caveats: Margins over OpenBLAS are 0.2-1% (within run-to-run noise) and TRMM is 13% slower, so this is parity rather than a speedup; numbers appear only in a chart image; matrix sizes, compiler, flags and OpenBLAS version are not stated; the bundled benchmark_cblas.py uses all-ones inputs and has no OpenBLAS harness (it can load another library via MUBLIS_LIB). x86 AVX2 results on Xeon Gold 6248R, Ryzen 7 7700X and i5-7500 are described as 'strong performance' without numbers. The same author's fast_matmul repo reportedly calls its kernel 'comparable' to OpenBLAS (not re-checked in this run).

notes: Chart numbers read directly from the image; the win is about 1% on GEMM and absent on TRMM, so record as parity with OpenBLAS (shortcoming: not meaningfully faster). Metadata verified: MIT, 2 stars, last commit 2026-09-01.

tier_reason: The README (and config.md, coverage.md, test/README.md, examples/README.md) state that ReLAPACK outperforms reference LAPACK and improves on OpenBLAS and MKL but give no numbers; the peer-reviewed paper that holds the measurements (arXiv:1602.06763, ACM TOMS Algorithm 979) could not be opened, so only a qualitative claim was seen.

corrections.stars_or_usage: 44 stars; vendored in OpenBLAS (relapack/ directory, optional build); published as ACM TOMS Algorithm 979
corrections.caveats: No numbers anywhere in the repo. The measurements are in Peise and Bientinesi, 'Recursive Algorithms for Dense Linear Algebra: The ReLAPACK Collection' (arXiv:1602.06763; web-search results give ACM TOMS 44(2), 16:1-16:19, 2017, as Algorithm 979), which this run could not open (arxiv.org, ar5iv, Semantic Scholar and the HPAC site are blocked); its abstract, seen in search snippets, says only that ReLAPACK 'clearly outperforms reference LAPACK, and even improves upon the performance of optimized libraries' in many scenarios. A check with access to the paper should raise the tier to B. Last commit is a 2022 typo fix; the code dates from 2016-2017 and was compared with OpenBLAS and MKL versions of that era. Linking with MKL requires COMPLEX_FUNCTIONS_AS_ROUTINES=1.

notes: Downgraded C to D because no numbers were visible on any reachable page; do not reject: it is notable (OpenBLAS ships a copy under relapack/, peer-reviewed TOMS algorithm). Recommend an Opus retier check against the arXiv paper, which likely yields B. Metadata verified: MIT, 44 stars, last commit 2022-02-20, abandoned.

tier_reason: First-party README plots (docs/images/spla_cosma_mkl.png, spla_cosma_libsci.png) with named CPUs/GPUs and a stated problem size, but no compiler, flags or benchmark program (examples/ holds only usage examples), so C.

corrections.claimed_speedup: README text: on CPU 'performance is much better compared to Intel MKL and similar to COSMA'; on GPU 'SPLA significantly outperforms COSMA and LIBSCI_ACC'. Plots (complex double PZGEMM-equivalent, M=N=10k, K=1M, block size 500), read from plot: CPU at 36 sockets SPLA about 0.305 vs MKL ScaLAPACK about 0.304 TFLOPS/socket (parity) and COSMA about 0.31; at 484 sockets SPLA about 0.26 vs MKL about 0.163 (about 1.6x) and COSMA about 0.235. GPU (host memory input) at 36 nodes SPLA about 4.0 vs COSMA about 2.6 vs LibSci_acc about 1.73 TFLOPS/node (about 2.3x over LibSci_acc); at 484 nodes about 1.65 vs 1.0 vs 0.27 (about 6x over LibSci_acc).
corrections.workload: Distributed tall-and-skinny complex matrix multiplication (pgemm_ssb stripe-stripe-block, expressed as an equivalent pzgemm call), M=N=10k, K=1M, block size 500, 36-484 sockets/nodes on Piz Daint: CPU nodes 2x18-core Xeon E5-2695 v4 (two ranks per node), GPU nodes Xeon E5-2690 v3 + Tesla P100 (one rank per node).
corrections.caveats: Plots only, no numeric speedups in the text (figures here are read from plots); compiler, flags and library versions not stated; no benchmark program found in examples/ (tests/ not inspected); one problem size; on CPU the MKL win appears only at higher socket counts (parity at 36 sockets) and COSMA is ahead of SPLA up to about 196 sockets; the GPU comparison does not include MKL; data from about 2020 on Piz Daint hardware.

notes: Numbers read from the two README plots; claims match. Metadata verified: BSD-3-Clause, 33 stars, last commit 2024-06-25 (stale).
